D5 — identity invariant)" - code: "rigorix-enterprise core/src/execution_api/application/catalog.rs:74 (MethodSpec) and :182 (dispatch); rigorix-oss server/src/rpc.rs (OSS dispatch)" - evidence: "`grep -rn 'auth.verify' rigorix-sdk/schemas rigorix-oss/{mcp,server}` → no hits (undeclared)" acceptance_criteria: - "[ ] `rigorix.auth.verify` is either declared in the frozen catalog (method + `$defs` + method-catalog.md) or removed — no undeclared `rigorix.*` remains" - "[ ] The verifier fails when a method list contains a name absent from `catalog.json` (a test proves it)" - "[ ] `catalog.json` documents that a server implements a subset (closed namespace)" - "[ ] CI green (fmt · clippy · test)" validators: [ci, architecture, canonical] implementation_notes: | - Match the existing naming style exactly: camelCase for multi-word methods (`rigorix.validatePlan`), dotted lowercase elsewhere. - `rigorix.auth.verify` is registered with `auth: Session`, `mcp_tool: None` and dispatches to claim verification (`self.claim.verify(scope, p)`) — an org-side JWKS verification of OSS-attested claims. # SDK-C5: Catalog parity — `rigorix.auth.verify` ## Problem The enterprise Execution API (rigorix-enterprise #206 / PR #208) registers `rigorix.auth.verify` as a **public JSON-RPC method**: - `core/src/execution_api/application/catalog.rs:74` — a `MethodSpec` (`auth: Session`, `mcp_tool: None`) - `:182` — a dispatch arm → claim verification (`self.claim.verify(scope, p)`) But it is absent from the frozen contract: - `schemas/api/catalog.json` — carries `rigorix.auth.login` / `.status` / `.logout` only - `schemas/api/method-catalog.md` — same Per **D-3** the catalog is the single source of truth for the shared `rigorix.*` namespace, so this is drift: an undeclared method in a namespace that is meant to be closed. Nothing catches it today — the conformance suite checks the claims/envelope *schemas*, not catalog parity. ## Evidence ``` $ grep -rn "auth\.verify" rigorix-sdk/schemas rigorix-oss/{mcp,server} (no hits) ``` `rigorix.validatePlan` (camelCase) is correctly declared, so naming is not the issue — only the missing declaration. ## Options 1. **Declare it** (contract-first): add `rigorix.auth.verify` + its `$defs` to `catalog.json` and `method-catalog.md`, described as the enterprise-side JWKS verification of OSS-attested claims. 2. **Fold it**: if it duplicates `rigorix.auth.status`, drop it and reuse the existing method. ## Recommendation Declare it if the enterprise genuinely needs an org-side claim-verification call distinct from session status (the `execution-api` module doc lists `rigorix.auth` as in scope); otherwise fold. Either way, add the **catalog-subset guard** so any future server-side method must be declared to pass CI. ## Canonical references - ADR-0001 (D-3 one catalog; D-5 identity invariant) - `rigorix-enterprise core/src/execution_api/application/catalog.rs:74` - `rigorix-oss server/src/rpc.rs` (OSS catalog dispatch) ## Acceptance Criteria | # | Criterion | Verify in | |---|-----------|-----------| | 1 | `rigorix.auth.verify` declared or removed — no undeclared `rigorix.*` | review | | 2 | Verifier rejects an undeclared method | unit | | 3 | Catalog documents the closed namespace | review | | 4 | CI green | CI |
title: SDK-C5: Catalog parity — declare `rigorix.auth.verify` (or fold it) + a catalog-subset conformance guard

Type generation can start before it; the e2e conformance run cannot." - name: "C1 SSE spec" type: internal note: "Client-side event stream consumption (optional for the first cut, required for parity)." intent: | Ship the first typed clients over the frozen `rigorix.*` catalog: a protocol-only Rust client and a TypeScript client. They are thin — request/result types mirror the catalog `$defs`, transport is JSON-RPC 2.0 over `POST /rpc`, errors map the `errors.json` taxonomy. Governance invariant (D-6): clients expose governed flows only; there is no raw step-execution method to wrap. Clients carry **no** engine dependency (D-1) — execution logic never moves into an SDK. in_scope: - "`rust/rigorix-client` (new crate in the `rust/` workspace): typed request/result structs for the catalog methods, JSON-RPC 2.0 transport (single + batch + notifications), error taxonomy mapping, device-flow auth helpers (`rigorix.auth.*`), `rigorix.system.version` negotiation" - "`typescript/` package: same surface, idiomatic TS types, fetch-based transport, error taxonomy mapping" - "Type source of truth = `schemas/api/catalog.json` `$defs` (+ `errors.json`); generated or hand-written with a drift test that fails if a catalog method has no client binding" - "Catalog-drift test: every `rigorix.*` method is either typed or explicitly listed as server-only (e.g. `rigorix.policy.bundle` is admin/enterprise)" - "Conformance: the Rust client drives one live run against C2 `rigorix-server` (plan → run → audit.read) and the result validates against the catalog result schema" - "README per client: transport, auth, the identity invariant (D5: caller identity fields are display-only)" out_of_scope: - Python / Java / Go clients (follow-up issues once Rust + TS are stable) - The verifier (`rust/rigorix-verifier`, already exists — protocol-only HMAC verification) - Any server change (C2 / C3) - Embedded/direct engine execution from a client (D-6 — Rust-only via `rigorix-engine`) - Automating releases/publishing to crates.io/npm (a separate packaging task) - A generated-vs-hand-written decision beyond "drift-tested against the catalog" affected_layers: clients: - "create: rust/rigorix-client/ (Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/types.rs, src/transport.rs, src/error.rs, src/auth.rs)" - "create: typescript/ (package.json, src/index.ts, src/types.ts, src/transport.ts, src/error.ts, tsconfig.json)" tests: - "create: rust/rigorix-client/tests/catalog_binding.rs (drift test)" - "create: rust/rigorix-client/tests/e2e_server.rs (against C2; ignored/skipped until C2 lands)" - "create: typescript/src/__tests__/ (transport + error mapping)" docs: - "create: rust/rigorix-client/README.md" - "create: typescript/README.md" - "modify: README.md (client inventory)" canonical_references: - adr: "docs/adr/ADR-0001-native-api-catalog.md — D2 (naming), D4 (auth levels), D5 (identity invariant), D6 (error model), D9 (MCP relationship), D10 (governed flows only)" - schema: "schemas/api/catalog.json — methods + $defs (the type source)" - schema: "schemas/api/errors.json — error taxonomy (data.type is the stable identifier)" - schema: "schemas/api/events.json — push payloads (C1); client event-stream binding" - code: "rust/rigorix-verifier — the protocol-only precedent crate (no engine dep)" - docs: "rigorix-oss docs/next-workstreams-2026-09-21.md §C4; docs/sdk-server-strategy-freeze-2026-09-06.md D-1/D-6" acceptance_criteria: - "`rust/rigorix-client` compiles and `cargo tree` shows NO `rigorix-engine` dependency (D-1 enforced in CI)" - "TypeScript client builds (`tsc`) and its tests pass" - "Drift test fails if a frozen catalog method has neither a typed binding nor an explicit server-only exemption" - "Error mapping test: each `errors.json` `data.type` maps to a distinct typed error; unknown types fall through to a generic error (never panic)" - "Batch request + notification framing tested (JSON-RPC array + no-`id`)" - "`rigorix.system.version` negotiation: the client exposes the constraints it requires" - "Live e2e (Rust → C2): plan → run → audit.read round-trips and validates against the result schema" - "No client surface exposes raw step execution (catalog scan / type review)" - "CI green (fmt · clippy · test)" validators: - ci - architecture - security - canonical implementation_notes: | - Reuse, don't invent: types MUST mirror `catalog.json` `$defs` field names exactly (serde field names tracked code-truth). If a shape is missing, the fix is a catalog change (contract change), not a client-local invention. - Keep the client transport dumb: JSON-RPC framing + auth header + error decode. # SDK-C4: Typed SDK clients against the frozen catalog (Rust + TypeScript) ## Intent Ship the first typed clients over the frozen `rigorix.*` catalog. Thin, protocol-only (no engine dep), governed-flows-only. Rust is the reference (mirrors `rigorix-verifier`); TypeScript proves the catalog is language-neutral. ## Dependencies ``` ADR-0001 (catalog freeze, done) │ ├──────────────► C4 typed clients (THIS ISSUE, rigorix-sdk) │ │ e2e needs │ ▼ └──────────────► C2 rigorix-server (rigorix-oss) ``` ## In Scope - `rust/rigorix-client` — typed methods, JSON-RPC transport, error mapping, device-flow auth helpers, version negotiation. - `typescript/` — same surface, idiomatic TS. - Catalog-drift test (every method bound or explicitly server-only). - Live e2e against C2 (Rust): plan → run → audit.read. - Per-client README (transport, auth, D5 invariant). ## Out of Scope - Python / Java / Go (follow-ups). - The verifier (exists). Server changes (C2/C3). - Embedded execution (D-6). Publishing/release automation. ## Affected Layers ### Clients - New: `rust/rigorix-client/` (lib, types, transport, error, auth) - New: `typescript/` (index, types, transport, error) ### Tests - New: `catalog_binding.rs` (drift), `e2e_server.rs` (gated on C2) - New: TS transport/error tests ### Docs - New: `rust/rigorix-client/README.md`, `typescript/README.md` ## Canonical References - **ADR-0001** — D2/D4/D5/D6/D9/D10 - **catalog** `schemas/api/catalog.json` (types) · **errors** `schemas/api/errors.json` - **precedent** `rust/rigorix-verifier` (protocol-only, no engine dep) - **backlog** `rigorix-oss docs/next-workstreams-2026-09-21.md` §C4 ## Acceptance Criteria | # | Criterion | Verify in | |---|-----------|-----------| | 1 | Rust client has NO `rigorix-engine` dep | `cargo tree` in CI | | 2 | TS client builds + tests pass | CI | | 3 | Drift test fails on an unbound catalog method | unit test | | 4 | Error taxonomy maps every `data.type`; unknown → generic (no panic) | unit test | | 5 | Batch + notification framing tested | unit test | | 6 | `rigorix.system.version` negotiation exposed | unit test | | 7 | Live e2e plan → run → audit.read validates | e2e (C2) | | 8 | No raw step-execution surface | review + drift test | | 9 | CI green | CI | ## Implementation Notes - **Reuse, don't invent.** Type fields mirror `catalog.json` `$defs` exactly. A missing shape is a catalog change, not a client-local type. - Transport stays dumb: framing + auth header + error decode. No policy logic. - D5: display-only identity fields must not be presented as authorization. - Model `rigorix-client` on `rust/rigorix-verifier` (protocol-only, no engine dep). - Gate the e2e test behind a server-URL env var so the crate is usable before C2. ## DoD - [ ] Rust + TS clients build/test green; no-engine-dep assertion in CI - [ ] Drift test green; all 19 methods bound or exempted - [ ] e2e against C2 green (once C2 merges) - [ ] READMEs written
title: SDK-C4: Typed SDK clients against the frozen catalog (Rust + TypeScript)
